questions.q: Who first suggested that the Doctor should become an animal-doctor?
choices: The Cat's-meat-Man
Polynesia
The old lame horse
His sister, Sarah
questions.evidence: Why don't you give up being a people's doctor, and be an animal-doctor?

questions.q: Who read the Doctor's book about cats to the Cat's-meat-Man?
choices: His son, who had learned to read at school
The Parson of Puddleby
His wife, Theodosia
Polynesia, sitting on the kitchen table
questions.evidence: my wife, Theodosia, she's a scholar

questions.q: How did the Doctor answer when the Cat's-meat-Man said he could make animals sick with something in their meat?
choices: He laughed and said it was a clever plan that would bring in plenty of money for them both
He said he would think about it and give an answer next week
He said quickly that the man must not do that because it would not be right
He said he could cure any animal no matter what had made it sick
questions.evidence: You mustn't do that. That wouldn't be right.

questions.q: According to Polynesia, what does "Ka-ka oi-ee, fee-fee?" mean in bird-language?
choices: "Where is the cracker you promised me?"
"Is the porridge hot yet?"
"Has it stopped raining?"
"Good morning, Doctor!"

questions.q: What did the Doctor do right after Polynesia told him that animals can talk?
choices: He went out into the garden in the pouring rain to listen to the birds there
He got the butcher's book and a pencil to write down bird words
He called Jip into the kitchen to test what the parrot said
He wrote a letter to the vet over the hill about it
questions.evidence: came back with the butcher's book and a pencil

questions.q: Why had Polynesia never spoken bird-language to the Doctor before?
choices: She was afraid he would tell other people her secret
She had forgotten most of it in all her years since leaving Africa
She thought he was too busy with his human patients
He would not have understood her, so there was no point
questions.evidence: You wouldn't have understood me if I had.

questions.q: When Jip twitched up one side of his nose, what was he asking?
choices: "When are you going to give me my supper tonight?"
"May I go out to play in the garden?"
"Can't you see that it has stopped raining?"
"Why is the parrot talking so much today?"
questions.evidence: Can't you see that it has stopped raining?

questions.q: Polynesia says animals talk "with their ears, with their feet, with their tails." What does she mean?
choices: Animals can only talk when they are moving around
Animals can send messages with their bodies, not only with sounds
Animals use their ears and tails to hear people and smell danger better
Animals have to learn to talk from parrots like her
questions.evidence: They talk with their ears, with their feet, with their tails--with everything.

questions.q: What did the plow-horse really need to fix his trouble?
choices: Big pills for his spavins
A new pair of horseshoes
Spectacles, because he was going blind in one eye
A long rest from plowing the big field
questions.evidence: I am going blind in one eye

questions.q: What color did the horse want his glasses to be?
choices: Blue, to match the sky
Green
Brown, like the Doctor's suit
Clear, like the Doctor's own pair

questions.q: Why did the horse kick the farmer's boy into the duck-pond?
choices: The boy tried to put a mustard-plaster on him
The boy had forgotten to give him his oats and water that morning
The boy was trying to take away his new green spectacles
The boy whipped him for plowing the field too slowly
questions.evidence: He tried to put a mustard-plaster on me last week.

questions.q: How did the Doctor make sure each kind of animal had its own way into the house?
choices: He set up a different waiting room in the garden for each animal
He saw horses on Mondays, cows on Tuesdays and sheep on Wednesdays each week
He had special doors made and wrote the kind of animal over each one
He let Polynesia call each animal in by name, one at a time
questions.evidence: he had to have special doors made for the different kinds

questions.q: How did animals in faraway lands come to hear about the Doctor?
choices: The Cat's-meat-Man wrote about him in the newspapers
Birds that flew to other countries in winter told them
The Doctor sailed to other countries to cure animals there
Polynesia sent letters to her old friends in Africa
questions.evidence: the birds who flew to other countries in the winter told the animals in foreign lands

questions.q: What is the one thing Polynesia says people have learned to understand in animal-language?
choices: That a cat purrs when it wants its dinner
That a horse stamps its feet when it is angry
That a dog wagging his tail means "I'm glad!"
That a parrot squawks when it is frightened
questions.evidence: when a dog wags his tail he means 'I'm glad!'

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: How the Cat's-meat-Man became the Doctor's best friend and helper
How Polynesia came to England from Africa long ago and saw King Charles hiding
How the Doctor learned animal-language and became a famous animal-doctor
How the farmers of Puddleby learned to put glasses on their horses
questions.evidence: the Doctor got to learn the language of the animals so well
